trigger: A session holding GuaranteedState:Read scoped to a management group (not global Infrastructure:Read) calls GET /api/v1/dex/app?name=<app> under RBAC enforcement.
policy_floor: routed-concerns.md Authentication/RBAC row: 'Every new list/fan-out read of per-agent data MUST use the admit-then-filter authorize_list_read chokepoint (World A, ADR-0017) -- never a bare global require_permission'
summary: GET /api/v1/dex/app always passed visible=nullptr to build_dex_app_model, so the devices[] affected-device list was never confined to the caller's management-group scope, unlike the equivalent /fragments/dex/app dashboard fragment (which applies resolve_visible/visible_set_fn). A confined operator saw fleet-wide device ids through this new REST route that the dashboard would have hidden from them.

trigger: guaranteed_state_store is null/unavailable when GET /api/v1/dex/devices/{id}/observations/{event_id} is called.
summary: Unlike every one of its 7 sibling DEX routes added in this same diff, this route had no explicit 'if (!guaranteed_state_store) 503' branch -- build_dex_observation_model folds a null store into nullopt, so a genuine service-unavailable condition rendered the SAME 404 'observation not found' as a real absence or foreign-device event, masking a storage-layer failure as a definitive not-found. The route's own already-shipped OpenAPI text already documented 503 for 'service unavailable' as a possible outcome; the code just didn't implement that path.

trigger: Same trigger as GOV-4035-5, via MCP tool get_dex_observation.
summary: MCP get_dex_observation had the identical missing-null-store-check gap as GOV-4035-5, returning kInvalidParams 'observation not found' instead of an internal-error response when the store is unavailable.

OpenAPI descriptions, MCP tool descriptions, and the changelog fragment for GET /dex/app, GET /dex/overview, get_dex_app, get_dex_overview described their device lists as unconditionally 'fleet-wide', which became stale the moment GOV-4035-1..4 were fixed. Updated in the same commit to state the lists are confined to the caller's management-group scope while the aggregate crash/health fields remain fleet-wide.
classification: wording (docs-writer domain), landed with the truth fix rather than a separate finding
